MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 17, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:04 p.m., on March 17, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 12, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:45 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:05
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

City Council Minutes  1  March 17, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Businesses of the Month - Restaurateur Salvatore Faso, Owner of Piccolino
  Ristorante, Delizie Ristorante, and The Modjeska Bar and Grill

  Mayor Kelley presented a proclamation to Salvatore Faso.

P2. Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Mira Folia and Jerry Silverstein
  for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center; and
  (2) Kathleen Mauzey, Jean Rogers, and Gary Schwarz for volunteer hours with the Mission
  Viejo Library.

P3. School Spotlight - Principal Bill Hinds, Los Alisos Intermediate

  The City Council received the presentation from Los Alisos Intermediate School Principal
  Bill Hinds.

P4. School Spotlight - Principal Laura Lyon, Castille Elementary

  The City Council received the presentation from Castille Elementary School Principal
  Laura Lyon.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Anna T. Boyce with blood drive volunteers Irena Cromwell, and Dan and Mary Lou Moncino,
M.V: announced that Mission Viejo received the American Red Cross Platinum Award for its
efforts with City's blood drive program. Mrs. Boyce noted that the next blood drive will be held
on April 25, 2014, from 12 noon to 6:00 p.m. at city hall.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed an audit he is conducting with the 2012 Improve Don't Move and
Commercial Fee Waiver programs and he questioned figures published in the City's 2012 Annual
Report.

Margo Ferron, M.V.: announced that this year's Relay for Life will be held June 7-8 at
Saddleback College. The City is going into the Relay with 5 major awards, including designation
as the #1 Relay in Orange County. Ms. Ferron thanked the City Council for always supporting
the Relay and she outlined events supporting and leading up to the Relay. Lastly, she directed
interested parties to www.mvrelay.org for more information.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reiterated his comments from the last Council Meeting regarding
statements made by former OCFA Chief Ron Blaul, more than two years ago in a public
meeting. Mr. Wontrobski asked if anyone on the City Council asked Chief Blaul to make those
statements and whether or not the public or staff had an opportunity to comment or rebut.

City Council Minutes  2  March 17, 2014
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3 and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 3, 2014, as presented.

4.  Check Register dated February 28, 2014 in the amount of $1,725,204.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2014

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for January 2014

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2014

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  March 17, 2014
 9.  General Plan Progress Report for 2013

  Received and filed.

11. Oso Parkway Widening, Interstate 5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  (1) Approved the plans and bid specifications subject to minor revisions required by the
  City Engineer, and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids; (2) authorized the
  issuance of a purchase order to VA Consulting, Inc., in the amount of $379,900.00 for
  additional design, bid, construction support, construction management, and inspection
  services related to the construction project.

NEW BUSINESS

13. Modification to Permit Parking Program on Boleada Drive, Consuelo Place, De La
  Luna Drive, Jacinto Drive, La Quilla Lane, Mirar Vista Drive, Poco Place, Oliva
  Place and Oso Rojo Lane

  Mark Chagnon, Director of Public Works, presented the staff report.

  The following expressed support for the proposed permit parking modification: Bob
  Watson, M.V.; Patty O'Connor, President of the Coronado Homeowners Association,
  M.V.; Al Holguin, M.V.; Robert Van der Capellen, M.V.; and Marlene Sais, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed permit parking modification: Doreen
  McKernan, M.V. and Dorothy Mowry, M.V.

  Written comments in opposition to the proposed modification to the permit parking
  program were received from the following: Nicole McKernan, M.V. and Ciara O'Reilly,
  M.V.

  Assistant Principal Todd Amon, Capistrano Valley High School, answered questions of the
  City Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 14-10 Modifying the Existing Permit Parking Program on Boleada Drive,
  Consuelo Place, De La Luna Drive, Jacinto Drive, La Quilla Lane, Mirar Vista Drive, Poco
  Place, Oliva Place and Oso Rojo Lane to include the Hours of 9:30 A.M. to 5:30 P.M.,
  Monday to Friday, September Through June, School Days Only.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  March 17, 2014
 RECESS

At the hour of 8:23 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:34
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Schlicht

20. Restroom Master Plan

  Council Member Schlicht presented her agenda report.

  The following made comments in support of the City installing restroom facilities in parks
  where sports are routinely played: Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Joe Tully, M.V.; Heidi Tully, M.V.;
  and Julia Tully, M.V.

  Staff answered the City Council Member's questions and the Council discussed the matter.

  There was no action taken.

OLD BUSINESS

12. First Amendment to the Law Enforcement Services Contract

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with the impact on total safety costs. He
  stated that police fees are about 25% of the City's budget and he suggested reducing
  overtime and retirement costs to free up money.

  Lt. Brad NewMyer answered the City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve the First
  Amendment to the FY 2013-2014 Law Enforcement Services Agreement by increasing the
  contract from $15,830,649 to $15,964,107 for costs associated with establishing two (2)
  Deputy Sheriff training positions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  March 17, 2014
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated February 21, 2014 in the Amount of $2,247,805.67

  Council Member Schlicht drew attention to a payment made to Robert Coffee Architects for
  Montanoso locker room facilities. She stated that there should be a public discussion to see
  if the Council really wants to go forward and spend the money on the project.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Second Amendment to the Construction and Demolition Waste Recycling Ordinance

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she removed this item from the Consent Calendar
  to stay consistent with her prior no vote.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to adopt
  Ordinance 14-302 Amending Paragraph (c) of Section 6.10.1140 of Division 10, Chapter
  6.10 of Title 6 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Relating to the Use of Diversion
  Performance Deposits.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: provided a timeline regarding the City of Irvine's consideration
  to withdraw from OCFA.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

15. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

City Council Minutes  6  March 17, 2014
 16. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

17. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

18. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg provided an update on the RFP for ambulance services. He stated that it is
unclear whether or not the City will have any input into the RFP process; a process that seems to
change on a daily basis. Last week County Counsel said that the RFP should not be released for
public comment but by the end of the day that recommendation was reversed. Mr. Wilberg noted
that the matter is scheduled to go to the County Board of Supervisors on April 7 or 8 and the City
will receive a copy when the agenda is distributed on March 27, at the earliest.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon reminded residents that the movie Behind the Orange Curtain will be
shown on Wednesday, March 17 at Casta del Sol at 7:00 p.m. Attendees can enter the
community at Gate 1 and let the guard know that they are there to see the movie. The film's
Producer, Natalie Costa, will be in attendance along with health care and drug enforcement
agency experts. Council Member Reardon announced that she and Tammy Descoteaux spent a
good part of the day last Wednesday at the South Orange County Coalition where the program
was all about prescription drug abuse. The event was held in Dana Point and she met consultant
Mike Darnold, who is a drug intervention specialist hired by the City of Dana Point to work with
the school district and the schools. When Mr. Darnold first started 5 years ago, he was primarily
serving kids who had been caught with drugs and now he is being called by parents to help them
address problems they are having with their kids. With his good work, they have reduced the
number of drug related offenses in the schools which, she noted, is a very good thing. Council
City Council Minutes  7  March 17, 2014
 Member Reardon discussed her attendance at firefighter Greg Hennessey's memorial service
with Mayor Kelly. She stated that it was very impressive to see people from all over paying
tribute to a very human man. She also outlined her attendance at a variety of events including
the Board of Supervisors Visionary Leaders conference, Rancho Mission Viejo Little League
opening day, the Mothers Against Drunk Driving awards banquet where Mission Viejo Deputy
Adam Sandler received an award for 124 DUI arrests in one year and, the Mayor's Prayer
breakfast on behalf of Mayor Kelley. Lastly, Council Member Reardon announced that she
cannot attend the dog park grand opening because she will be away at a retreat.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht thanked Lt. Brad NewMyer for his out of the box thinking but she
voted no on agenda item 12 because of the increase in costs that the Council has seen in so many
areas. She stated that she appreciates the Lieutenant's proactive approach in trying to fill
vacancies but it's a countywide problem and she thinks it needs to be remedied there. Council
Member Schlicht stated that the Council needs to return local control and allow the Community
Services Commission, who are appointed Mission Viejo residents, to have input and public
forums for a lot of the CIPS because most of the time they are all staff-driven. She feels that
there is not much opportunity for change once a project comes to the Council and she stated that
the City Council has pretty much lost control of what needs to be done, in her opinion. Council
Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at last month's joint SOC 912 and Saddleback
Republican Assembly meeting with guest speaker Loren Spivak whose Free Market Warrior
store was expelled from a mall in North Carolina for selling material critical of the Obama
administration. She observed that Simon, the owner of the Shops at Mission Viejo, also owns
the North Carolina mall and she noted the irony that we have a conservative city but there are
liberals trying to control the public. Council Member Schlicht announced that the next meeting
of SOC 912, will be held on Friday March 21 at the Norman P. Murray Community Center at
7:00 p.m. with guest speaker Kelly Hubbard, author of the OC Tea Party blog who will talk
about the June candidates. On March 20, at 7:00 p.m. the Saddleback Republican Assembly will
host guest speaker Robert Ming, Board of Supervisor 5th district candidate. She stated that
everyone is invited to attend and she encouraged people to take a proactive approach in who they
are voting for. She also mentioned her attendance at Robert Ming's March 8 campaign
headquarters grand opening and she discussed the Common Core curriculum which, she said, is
actually taking parental authority away from the parents and making children believe that
government is their caretaker. She further discussed her attendance at a meet and greet event for
John Moorlach who withdrew from his congressional race because he did not have established
GOP support. Council Member Schlicht stated that she is one of the lucky ones because of grass
roots support and she noted that she is not influenced by special interests. She also gave a shout
out to Mission Viejo High School which was rated one of the top Orange County high schools in
an Orange County Register poll and she encouraged residents to read the March issue of the
Community Common Sense newspaper. Council Member Schlicht said that it is important to
start realizing that we have kind of lost our constitution and the rule of law and people need to
start getting personally involved and they can make a difference. In that spirit, she read a quote
from Thomas Jefferson: "On every question of construction let us carry ourselves back to the
time when the Constitution was adopted, recollect the spirit manifested in the debates, and

City Council Minutes  8  March 17, 2014
 instead of trying what meaning may be squeezed out of the text, or intended against it, conform
to the probable one in which it was passed."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury discussed his attendance at the morning session of the Visionary Leaders
conference where he heard the head of the United Way of Orange County speaking. He noted
that there seems to be coalescing of a lot of philanthropic organizations, but there is a lack of
faith-based organizations and he has provided that input to those running the
organizations. Council Member Ury announced that he attended the South Orange County
Regional Chamber of Commerce and South Orange County Economic Coalition talent show
where he had the chance to be in a barbershop quartet and he noted that he had a really good
time.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that Council Member Ury did a great job in the talent show and
it was a really fun event with a lot of good acts. He announced that Richard Smith and Julie
Adams will perform with the Lord of the Strings on April 5 in the Council Chamber at 7:00
p.m. He also thanked staff for planning the grand opening of La Paws Park on April 12 and he
noted that he stopped by the dog park the other day and he couldn't believe what has transpired
there over the months. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness discussed the speech he gave at Mount of
Olives Church yesterday and he thanked staff member Karen Wylie for setting him up with gold
plated shovels, ribbon and a giant set of scissors for the grand opening of the church's new
building. Mr. Leckness noted in his speech that the church is ground zero of Mission Viejo
because founders of the area threw a rock in the air and built the first church where the rock
landed. Karen Wylie gave him historic photos of Mission Viejo which show the church and
nothing else around it and he stated that he really enjoyed being part of the event. Council
Member Reardon added that Acoustic Eidolon will perform in the Council Chamber on
Saturday, March 22 at 7:00 p.m.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that the City has again been affirmed with a AAA credit rating by
Standard & Poor's. The rating indicates that Mission Viejo has an extremely strong capacity to
meet its financial commitments and it is based on a strong local economy, high incomes and
housing values, balanced budgets, strong reserves, fully funded annual pension contributions and
a strong debt profile. She noted that there are only 6 other cities in Orange County that have
received the AAA rating and she commended the City Manager and staff on a job well
done. Mayor Kelley introduced the City's new Orange County Register reporter, Brooke
Staggs. She welcomed Ms. Staggs and encouraged her to contact the Council Members so she
can begin reporting on the good things going on in Mission Viejo. Mayor Kelley disused her
attendance at the kick-off event for a recycling campaign at Mission Viejo High School which is
put on by the organization, Help Our Plant. The City was able to assist by donating recycle
containers which were purchased with grant funding and CR&R is also helping. She also
attended, with Council Member Reardon, the U.S. Tennis Association awards program where
City Council Minutes  9  March 17, 2014
 she was pleased to receive the Brad Parks Award on behalf of the City for hosting the
Wheelchair Tennis Masters and for supporting wheelchair tennis over the years. She commended
Steve Bell and staff for their work with the tennis tournament and Jason Harnett for his coaching
and service to the wheelchair tennis community. Mayor Kelley reminded residents that Up in the
Air, hosted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee, will be held on Saturday, March 22 at
Oso Viejo Park and she encouraged everyone to attend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 7, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 7, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  March 17, 2014
